Fabric Design · Lecture 17

Stripe and Check Designs

Combining weaves side by side (stripes) and in both directions (checks); the 36-end turned-twill check and the warp/weft-face combination.
StripeCheckTwill turnedFace combination

Rules for combining weaves

Weaves can be placed side by side when they have the same number of picks in the repeat (or a common multiple) and interlace with similar frequency, so that the fabric does not pucker. At the join, warp floats of one weave should meet weft floats of the other to make a clean cut. A stripe changes weave across the ends; a check changes it across picks as well.

Stripe: 2/2 twill Z beside 2/2 twill S · 16 ends × 8 picks
